result.note: Tested the RBI's October 2026 rate hike, stance and forecasts, and the opposition protest against the CEC alongside the Supreme Court hearing on the voter-roll drive.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision in October 2026:
items: It raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, its first hike in nearly four years.
It shifted its policy stance to "calibrated tightening".
It lowered its FY27 growth forecast to 7.1%.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong because the RBI nudged its FY27 growth forecast up to 7.1%, while lifting its inflation forecast to 5.2%. The shift signals that imported oil and a weak monsoon worry the central bank more than demand does.
questions.source: It lifted its FY27 inflation forecast to 5.2% while nudging growth up to 7.1%, signalling that imported oil and a weak monsoon now worry it more than demand does.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, opposition MPs protested over a contested voter-roll revision. Consider the following statements:
items: The MPs marched from Parliament to the Election Commission demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign.
The Supreme Court agreed to hear challenges to the voter-roll revision drive.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct: police detained the marching MPs, including Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and the Supreme Court agreed the same week to hear challenges to the drive. Removing the CEC needs a parliamentary majority the opposition lacks, so the court is its likelier route.
questions.source: Removing Kumar needs a parliamentary majority the opposition lacks, so the Supreme Court, which agreed this week to hear challenges to the voter drive, is the likelier route to any win they can claim.
